goal: Prevent memory exhaustion attacks where peers send millions of tiny witness items in blocks or transactions
Reject oversized or empty transactions upfront during deserialization rather than allocating buffer memory
agreement: Wide concept approval across contributors and maintainers
Verified clean allocation drops and passing unit tests (Yudis-bit)
Unaddressed objection: makes witness verification costlier without deferred copying (fametrano)
Nonblocking objection: touches 76 files before abstracting transaction access (purpleKarrot)
Noted transient build slowdown with byte loops on GCC 13.3 (instagibbs)

categories.name: p2p
why: P2 because it enforces upfront message bounds against peers sending pathological witness data
Drops deserialized memory for malicious blocks from over 90 MiB to under 4 MiB

categories.name: validation
why: P2 because it removes a key resource-exhaustion vector during block deserialization
Reduces pathological block deserialization time from 279 ms to 19 ms and peak memory to under 8 MiB
